agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — no live-preview mechanism exists in the codebase. The useContent hook (236 callers) and the contentstack service layer are the attachment points. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. Contentstack is unreachable at test time, so VCs that depend on it are framed with the boundary assumption.

Openspec provided empty acceptance criteria, so all 18 ACs are original to this review. I was unable to read the four referenced files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) which would have informed boundary assumptions and integration-point specifics — the ACs are framed as observable outcomes from the story description alone. Key areas covered: core real-time update behavior (AC-1), brand coverage across GO/UP/MX (AC-2–4), connection resilience and reconnection (AC-5–6), error handling for unreachable Contentstack and timeouts (AC-7–8), concurrent editing (AC-9), rich content types including linked references (AC-10), security — credential leakage and XSS (AC-11–12), accessibility — WCAG 2.1 AA and live region announcements (AC-13–14), session persistence on navigation (AC-15), content lifecycle — unpublished/deleted entries (AC-16), graceful degradation for unsupported browsers (AC-17), and performance under rapid updates (AC-18).

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec's contribution was marginal: it identified attachment points (useContent hook, contentstack service layer) and framed boundary assumptions, but did not produce acceptance criteria — leaving speckit to author all 18 ACs from scratch. Speckit provided comprehensive coverage (real-time behavior, brand variants, resilience, security, accessibility, performance) but explicitly could not read the four referenced source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), meaning ACs lack integration-point specificity and may miss concrete boundary conditions. The two agents added non-overlapping but also non-collaborative value — openspec's context notes were not incorporated into speckit's ACs since speckit could not access the source files openspec referenced. 18 ACs for a single story with broad scope (real-time updates across 3 brands, security, accessibility, degradation, lifecycle) strongly suggests a story split was warranted, yet neither agent proposed one. The pipeline failed to achieve its intended sequential elaboration-then-review pattern; instead it produced context notes followed by blind AC authoring. Human review needed to: (1) validate ACs against actual source code, (2) determine if story should be split into 2-3 stories, (3) confirm boundary assumptions around Contentstack unreachability are correct.
